title: [D8 Guardrails] Secrets hygiene and key-in-URL redaction tests
summary: `tests/test_secrets.py` is the five channels `concept/07` names, for the ones that had no owner: the path form of a loader's stored fetch trace and of its stored failure detail, the secret wrapper as a property of the package (no model field can hold a credential without the redacting serializer, every such model hides the input in its errors, and `reveal()` is called in three declared places), source control over every tracked file including fixtures, and the two downstream surfaces a prompt test cannot reach -- a stored evidence row and an emitted message. 17 tests. It found two open channels rather than confirming none: `load_threatfox` stored its fetch diagnostic unredacted, and `http.client.InvalidURL` escaped both fetch functions untyped and printed the request path into a traceback. Both are fixed in `src/helena/enrichment.py`; `docs/runbook.md` §14 documents the two exposure profiles with the measurements re-taken 2026-09-12.
assumption_validated: That the asymmetry is real and that writing the guardrail against the LIVE key rather than a placeholder is what makes it worth writing. Both held, and the second held harder than expected. Measured against abuse.ch 2026-09-12: the bulk export the loader fetches answers 200 with no credential, the hunting API answers 401 without an `Auth-Key` header and 200 with it, and the v2 export at `threatfox-api.abuse.ch/v2/files/exports/<AUTH-KEY>/full.csv.zip` answers 401 for a key that is not one -- so the path segment really is the credential, and only that profile needs the URL rule. The negative result is the valuable one: the first run of the new exception test printed the real abuse.ch key into this session's terminal, because `http.client.InvalidURL` is a subclass of neither `OSError` nor `ValueError` and so was not caught by either fetch function's typed-failure wrapper. A placeholder key would have produced the same traceback and nobody would have looked twice.
makes_buildable: Task 52's end-to-end fixture run inherits a credential story that is enforced rather than asserted: a loader cannot be called without a redactor, a fetch failure cannot raise an unredacted message, no model can hold a credential without the serializer, and a committed file carrying a live value is a named test failure. `keyed_context` in the module is also a reusable one-fixture way to build a real enriched context whose provenance URL carried a key, which is what any later provider or feed increment needs to prove the same property for itself.

verification.detail: 1810 passed in 786 s, the whole suite, run twice. The first run was 1809 passed, 1 skipped -- the skip was `tests/test_analyst.py:1725`, the live analyst run whose configured model returned `schema_invalid` that time and passed the next, which is model behaviour rather than this increment's (task 50's baseline was 1793 passed). Two comment-only edits landed during the second run -- a prose paragraph in `docs/runbook.md` §14 and the re-measurement dates in `helena.enrichment`'s ThreatFox section head -- so the final tree was re-verified with `tests/test_secrets.py tests/test_enrichment.py tests/test_threatfox.py` (81 passed in 52 s) and `-m conformance` (27 passed in 32 s). `uv run pytest -q tests/test_secrets.py` alone is 17 passed in 33 s, `uv lock --check` resolves 17 packages unchanged and `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` is clean. Seven of the 17 run against the real engine over a real capture and the committed ThreatFox extract. THE LIVE MEASUREMENTS, 2026-09-12, by status code and never by printing a value: `GET threatfox.abuse.ch/export/json/recent/` 200 with no credential; `POST threatfox-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/` 401 with no `Auth-Key` header and 200 with one; `GET threatfox-api.abuse.ch/v2/files/exports/<a key that is not one>/full.csv.zip` 401, which is what makes the path segment the credential. SIX GATE MUTATIONS WERE INDUCED, OBSERVED RED AND REVERTED, `git status` clean after each: (1) `http.client.HTTPException` removed from `_FETCH_FAILURES` -> five tests red, including the stored-trace and the live-key ones; (2) `from None` -> `from failure` -> the two exception tests red on the restored chain; (3) the redactor dropped from the fetch message -> the two exception tests red while the three store-level tests stayed green, which is how the two redaction layers were shown to cover different surfaces rather than to duplicate each other; (4) one `SecretField` annotation narrowed to `Secret` -> the serializer test red; (5) `hide_input_in_errors=True` deleted from the settings model config -> that test red naming both models; (6) a fourth `reveal()` call added to `src/helena/status.py` -> the declared-callers test red. The repository scan was proved to read staged bytes the same way: a file holding `ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY=<40 hex characters that are not a key>` was `git add -N`ed, the shape test went red naming it, and the file was removed from the index and the disk.

escalations.detail: `helena.enrichment.fetch_threatfox` and `fetch_public_suffix_list` now take a REQUIRED keyword-only `redactor`. Not an escalation under `concept/instruction.md` §3 -- no dependency, no store, no contract field, no stored column added or renamed -- and both are called only by their own loaders, which already hold a redactor. Recorded here because it is a public signature in `__all__` and because one stored value changes shape: a `failed` row of `helena_reference_feed_snapshot` now carries a redacted `failure_detail` where before it carried the raw message. No migration, no schema change.

Both fetch functions raise `from None` rather than `from failure`, so the original exception's frames are no longer in the traceback. Deliberate: a traceback printer prints the `__cause__` chain in full, so a redacted message over an unredacted cause is not redacted, and `urllib`'s exceptions build their `str()` from attributes rather than `args`, so sanitizing the caught exception in place does not work (`HTTPError.__str__` reads `code` and `reason`). What is kept is the original's type name and message inside the typed error, which is also what the loader stores. If a future session needs the frames back, the redaction has to move somewhere that still covers an escaping exception -- not back to `from failure`.

THE LIVE ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY WAS PRINTED INTO THIS SESSION'S TRANSCRIPT by a pytest traceback before the fix (the escaping `InvalidURL`, described above). Checked afterwards: no file on disk holds any configured credential -- not `prds/logs/task-51-*`, not `.pytest_cache`, not `.run`, and the runner's log envelope carries only the session's final message, which does not quote it. Nothing is committed and nothing needs rewriting. The value is still in the agent transcript outside the repository, so rotating `ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY` at abuse.ch is the cautious call and is the operator's to make; `docs/runbook.md` §14 has the order to do it in.

invariant_conflicts.detail: The task says *"the bulk export carries the key in the URL path ... while the API carries it in a header"*. That is the claim `concept/05` corrected on 2026-09-03 and records as having been wrong, and it is wrong again today: the bulk export the loader fetches needs no credential at all. The accurate version was implemented -- the two profiles live on TWO DIFFERENT ENDPOINTS, the path one is a v2 export nothing here fetches, and the bulk export has neither profile -- and `docs/runbook.md` §14 carries a `Do not "re-correct" the 2026-09-03 correction` paragraph, because this claim has already flip-flopped through four files once. The task's conclusion survives unchanged: one profile needs the URL rule and the other does not.

deferred: The Pydantic-dump half of step 3 is not restated here. `tests/test_config.py` already asserts `model_dump` and `model_dump_json` over `ProviderCredentials` and over a whole `Settings` including the real `.env`, and a second definition of one property is worse than none. What this module adds instead is the package-wide structural version -- every model field annotated with a secret uses `SecretField`, every model holding one sets `hide_input_in_errors=True`, and `reveal()` is called in three declared places -- which is what makes the wrapper a property of the package rather than of the two models that happen to exist.

The log channel, the agent-visible tool surface and the prompt bytes are likewise not restated; `tests/test_observability.py`, `tests/test_tools.py` and MNH-15 own them against the live key, and the module header has the table. MNH-15's docstring and `COVERED_BY` were updated to name this module instead of 'task 51'.

The credential-shaped repository scan is NOT exhaustive and does not claim to be. It fires on a credential-named key assigned an opaque value, and on a URL carrying userinfo; a key pasted into prose with no name beside it is invisible to it. What covers that case is the live-value scan beside it (every tracked file, every value the local `.env` holds) plus `.gitignore`, and an entropy or length heuristic was deliberately not used for the reason task 02 recorded: this project's URLs have sha256 path segments, and a heuristic would fire on provenance.

No `secrets` pytest marker and no `make secrets`. The 17 tests are 33 s inside `make check`; the `conformance` marker exists because an operator asks that question directly, and this is not a second such question.

`src/helena/migrations.py` stores `str(error)` as a migration note without a redactor. Left alone: a psycopg error for a failed statement carries the SQL, not the DSN, and the migration runner holds no `Secret` at all -- giving it a redactor would be a credential path where there is none. Named here so the next session does not read its absence as an oversight.
lessons: `http.client.InvalidURL` IS A SUBCLASS OF NEITHER `OSError` NOR `ValueError`, so `except (URLError, OSError, ValueError)` -- the tuple both of this project's fetch functions used -- does not catch it. It is raised by `putrequest` for a path containing a space, BEFORE the connection is opened (4 ms against a host that does not resolve, so it is hermetic and usable in a test), and its message quotes the whole request path. That is the one exception type whose `str()` carries the URL, which narrows `docs/decisions/0005`'s 'str(exception) does not' -- amended there rather than left to be rediscovered.

REDACTING AN EXCEPTION'S MESSAGE IS HALF THE JOB; THE CHAIN IS THE OTHER HALF. `raise Typed(redactor.text(...)) from failure` still leaks, because every traceback printer prints `__cause__` in full. Sanitizing the caught exception in place does not work either: `urllib.error.HTTPError.__str__` is built from `code` and `reason`, not from `args`, so rewriting `args` changes nothing. `from None` is what closes it, at the cost of the original's frames.

THE TWO REDACTION LAYERS ON A LOADER COVER DIFFERENT SURFACES AND THAT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Removing the redactor from the fetch message leaves the three stored-row tests GREEN (the loader redacts again before storing) and turns the two exception tests red; removing it from the store would leave the exception tests green. So neither is a duplicate of the other: one protects the in-flight exception, which no logger sees, and one protects the stored provenance column, which covers every `ThreatFoxError` the parse can raise as well.

A REPOSITORY SCAN FOR CREDENTIALS SHOULD BE TWO TESTS, NOT ONE. The live-value scan over `git ls-files` is exact and is the one that matches the incident behind the rule (a key inside a pasted link); the shaped scan is for a value this `.env` does not hold, and it works because the suite's placeholders already name themselves (`abusech-key-under-test`) -- so the rule is 'a credential-shaped value must say it is not real' rather than an allowlist someone has to extend. Measured over the tree: 12 candidate values, of which 6 are attribute expressions or variable names filtered by shape, and the remaining 6 are the suite's own placeholders.

ASSERT THAT A SCAN REACHED SOMETHING. Both repository tests assert a floor on what they read (200+ tracked files, 5+ fixtures), and the message test asserts the schema walk found `assessment_id`/`caveat`/`native_evidence`/`disclosed_to` before asserting no URL-shaped field exists. A scan that silently reads nothing passes every 'X is absent' assertion it makes.

`git add -N` IS HOW TO MUTATION-TEST A `git ls-files` GATE. The planted file becomes tracked for the scan without being committed, and `git rm --cached` plus `rm` reverts it. The planted value must be a fake -- never the live one -- because the failure message names what it found.
failed_approaches: Using a real abuse.ch host for the exception test. The InvalidURL path is validated in `putrequest`, which happens before `connect()`, so a host that does not resolve (`feed.invalid`) raises the same exception in 4 ms with no network at all. Pointing it at the real host would have opened a TCP connection for nothing, and a test that needs the network to raise is a test that goes red when the network does.

A `\n`-terminated URL as the way to make `urllib` quote the path. Measured: the trailing newline is stripped before the path is validated and the request goes through to the real host (200/401), so that shape proves nothing. A space in the segment AFTER the key is the one that raises, and it is also the one that shows the bound cutting through a credential.

An entropy or length heuristic over every string in the repository for the credential-shaped scan. Rejected before it was written, for task 02's reason: this project fetches URLs whose path segments are sha256 hashes and whose fixtures are full of 64-character digests and identifiers, so the heuristic's hits would be provenance and its misses would be anybody's guess. The scan fires on the NAME BESIDE THE VALUE, which a pasted configuration line has and a digest does not.

Asserting `reveal()` call counts per module rather than the set of modules. A second legitimate provider in `helena.providers` would add a second call and break a count for no reason; what matters is WHICH modules a credential travels through. The test asserts the set and the docstring says why.

Keying the declared-`reveal()` map by file basename. Changed to repository-relative paths before committing: `scripts/` is scanned too, so a basename collision between a script and a module would have masked a call rather than reported it.
next_session_should_know: Secrets hygiene is a suite now, and it bit twice on the way in. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE TWO EXPOSURE PROFILES ARE TWO ENDPOINTS, NOT TWO READINGS OF ONE. The hunting API takes the key in an `Auth-Key` HEADER; the v2 export takes it in a URL PATH and nothing here fetches it; the bulk export the loader does fetch needs NO credential, re-measured 2026-09-12. `docs/runbook.md` §14 is the table, the measurements and the `do not re-correct the correction` warning. The task description for task 51 carried the pre-2026-09-03 error and is recorded in `invariant_conflicts` -- if a later task's text repeats it, the note is wrong and §14 is right, and `concept/05` records the whole history. (2) A LOADER FETCH CANNOT BE CALLED WITHOUT A REDACTOR. `fetch_threatfox(url, redactor=...)` and `fetch_public_suffix_list(url, redactor=...)` are keyword-only and required, they build their typed message through `Redactor.text`, and they raise `from None`. If you add a third fetch, copy all three properties; `_FETCH_FAILURES` is the tuple to catch and it includes `http.client.HTTPException` for the reason in its comment. (3) `http.client.InvalidURL` ESCAPES `except (URLError, OSError, ValueError)`. It is a subclass of neither, it quotes the request path in its message, and it is raised before the connection opens -- which is why it is the cheapest hermetic way to make a fetch fail in a test, and why it was able to print a live key into a traceback with nothing logged. `docs/decisions/0005` has the amendment. (4) THE THREE AST GATES WILL FAIL ON NEW CODE, AND EACH FAILURE IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OBSTACLE. A model field annotated `Secret` instead of `SecretField` is red; a model holding a `SecretField` without `hide_input_in_errors=True` is red; a FOURTH module calling `reveal()` is red, and `REVEALED_IN` in `tests/test_secrets.py` is the declared three (`providers.py` for the `Auth-Key` header, `agents.py` for the `Bearer` header, `observability.py` for registering values with the redactor). `scripts/` is scanned as well, because a script that reveals a key is the shell-history channel. (5) A NEW TEST CREDENTIAL HAS TO NAME ITSELF. `test_every_credential_shaped_value_in_a_committed_file_says_it_is_not_real` requires any credential-shaped literal in a tracked file to contain one of `NOT_REAL` -- `under-test`, `conformance`, `fake`, `example`, `placeholder`, `redacted`, `invalid`, `sample`, `dummy`. Follow the suite's existing convention (`abusech-key-under-test`) and it never fires. A URL with userinfo is judged by its HOST for the same reason, because the redaction tests legitimately feed such URLs in. (6) `keyed_context` IS A REUSABLE REAL-PIPELINE FIXTURE: the committed capture through the real normalizer, the committed ThreatFox extract through the real loader, with the live key in the load's URL path, and it returns `(connection, snapshot, matched_entity, key)`. The final test walks prompt, evidence rows and emitted message off it; anything that needs 'a real context whose provenance carried a credential' should take it rather than rebuild one. (7) THE EMITTED MESSAGE HAS NO URL-SHAPED FIELD AND THAT IS NOW ASSERTED. `URL_SHAPED` is checked against the recursive JSON Schema of `sink.OutputMessage`, so adding a `source_url`, `endpoint` or `link` to the message is red -- and the right reading of that failure is that a key in a path has just been given somewhere to arrive, not that the test needs widening. `EmittedDisclosure.disclosed_to` is a host for the same reason, which `helena.policy` already enforces at load.
